Here's what just happened with Anthropic

Anthropic (the company that makes Claude AI) launched Claude Fable 5 on June 9, 2026. It's one of its newest and strongest AI models yet. Think of it as a super-smart version of Claude that’s really good at things like:

- Writing and fixing computer code (software engineering)
- 
Handling big knowledge work, research, and analysis
Understanding images and vision tasks

It shares the same powerful base as its even more advanced Claude Mythos 5 model. The big difference? 

Fable 5 has extra safety locks built in for risky topics (like advanced cybersecurity or biology stuff). If you ask something dangerous, it switches to an older, safer model instead of answering fully. 

Mythos 5 has fewer of those locks and was only for trusted partners at first.

People who tried it said it was a huge jump – it could work on long tasks for days and beat other top AIs on many tests.

US government pulled Anthropic's two most powerful models offline

Fable 5 and Mythos 5 are gone, citing national security

Reason: a jailbreak that Anthropic says is narrow, non-universal, and already possible with literally every other model including GPT-5.5

So the government found a minor vulnerability that exists across the entire industry

And instead of a fix, the response was just to shut it all down

Anthropic statement: if this standard applied to everyone, no frontier model would ever ship again 

My concern is that fable 5 already had a built in safety layer which makes it automatically switch to Opus models

So what exactly are they pausing here?

Is this about safety? or is this about control over who gets to build the most powerful AI?

data.text:
⚡️ US Government Shuts Down Claude Fable 5 Just 4 Days After Launch

US authorities decided the AI's security systems had been compromised and demanded that access be cut off for all non-US users, including Anthropic's own foreign employees.

Instead, the company took a different approach — it shut down Fable 5 and Mythos 5 (which hadn't even launched publicly) completely and started investigating what the government had found.
